summary: Shohei Ohtani agreed to a 10-year, $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers, the largest in North American team sports history, as announced by CAA and by Ohtani on Instagram. The note covers how the deal compares with other record contracts, how deferrals help the Dodgers with luxury-tax calculations, and Ohtani's elbow surgery that will keep him from pitching in 2024. It also reviews his career achievements and his desire to reach the postseason, which he has never done.
one_line: Shohei Ohtani signs a record 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers, though he will not pitch in 2024 after elbow surgery.
key_facts: Shohei Ohtani agreed to a 10-year, $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers, announced by his agency CAA on Saturday, the largest in major North American team sports.
Ohtani is 29 years old and has played in MLB since the 2018 season after leaving Japan.
The deal tops the $360 million free-agent record set by Aaron Judge and the $426.5 million extension of Mike Trout.
It also exceeds Patrick Mahomes' $450 million contract and Lionel Messi's $674 million contract signed in 2017 with FC Barcelona.
Deferrals lower the average annual value of Ohtani's deal, helping the Dodgers manage MLB's luxury-tax system.
Mookie Betts has $115 million deferred in his 12-year, $365 million Dodgers contract, lowering his average annual value from $30.4 million to $25.5 million.

Ohtani will not pitch in 2024 as he recovers from a September operation on his right elbow's ulnar collateral ligament; he had Tommy John surgery in 2018, and the Los Angeles Times reported the second surgery was also a Tommy John procedure.
Ohtani plans to attempt a return to the mound in 2025, and his agent Nez Balelo said "Shohei loves to pitch."
Ohtani won the American League Rookie of the Year in 2018 and the American League MVP in two of the past three seasons.
In 2023 Ohtani made 23 starts with a 3.14 ERA, hit 44 homers, and had a career-best 1.066 OPS, leading the AL in homers, on-base percentage and slugging percentage.
He closed the World Baseball Classic final for Japan by striking out Mike Trout, and his four-seam fastball averaged nearly 97 mph in 2023.
The Dodgers have won the NL West in 10 of the past 11 seasons and won the World Series in 2020; Ohtani has never played a postseason game.
